cluster_name: Twin mass shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town kill 27
event_summary: Eight gunmen stormed a bar in Wedela township near Johannesburg on 26 September 2026, killing 17 and wounding 15; hours later gunmen killed 10 and wounded 11 at a venue in Lwandle near Cape Town. No arrests had been made in either case by Sunday.
tldr: All 20 headlines across 12 countries converge on a single factual hook: two simultaneous mass shootings, 27 dead. The headline layer adds almost no interpretive framing beyond the body count — structural cause (gang turf, illegal mining), systemic context (South Africa's murder rate), and policy response (military deployment) that dominate body coverage are entirely absent at the homepage layer. South China Morning Post is the sole outlier, uniquely embedding electoral politics in its title with the phrase 'as elections near.'

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to embed electoral framing in its headline ('27 dead as elections near'), making upcoming South African elections a visible contextual hook absent from all other titles.

Only outlet to report a partial toll (17 dead) rather than the combined 27, foregrounding the Johannesburg tavern shooting alone — an artifact of early publication before the Cape Town count was confirmed.
Only headline to append 'gunmen on the run', shifting the advertised frame from a concluded atrocity to an active fugitive threat.
Sole headline to append '(VIDEOS)' as a multimedia call-to-action, the only outlet to use headline space for engagement cues rather than factual reporting.

bottom_line: The headline layer for the South Africa shootings is almost entirely uniform: 19 of 20 outlets reduced the story to a death toll and agent (gunmen, 27 dead), with manhunt language the only editorial variation; South China Morning Post is the sole outlier inserting electoral context, a frame absent from every other homepage.
